Mechanical export via Playwright/Chromium per step_10/PROMPT.md: page.goto() the file's own file:// path, awaited document.fonts.ready, called page.emulate_media(media='screen') immediately before page.pdf() (the standing fix for Chromium's print-media Devanagari pre-base-vowel-reordering bug), and used print_background=True + prefer_css_page_size=True (no explicit format/width/height) so the base CSS's own @page/A4/9mm-margin rules govern pagination. First export attempt produced 9 pages with a genuinely BLANK final page (0 extracted chars) - a real hard-gate failure, not accepted. Root-caused: forcing page.emulate_media('screen') for the Devanagari fix means the @media print rule that normally zeros .sheet's 9mm padding never fires; padding on a fragmented/paginated box only shows at the very start (top of page 1) and very end (bottom of the last page) of the whole flowed box, not on every page. This chapter's total content height happened to land only a little past a clean page boundary (q_13.10, the last item, fills its page almost to the bottom edge, confirmed by direct visual inspection) - the extra ~9mm of otherwise-harmless trailing .sheet padding was just enough to push a near-empty remainder onto a genuinely blank 9th page. Fixed with one added, narrowly-scoped CSS rule in this chapter's own 09_design/final.hi.css (`.sheet { padding-bottom: 0; }`, documented in place) - zeros only the bottom padding (top/left/right untouched, so the on-screen page opens with its normal margin, no visual change anywhere actual content is) and does not touch any content. Re-exported: page count dropped to 8 with zero blank pages; visually re-confirmed both the first page (title/ex_13.1-13.3, unchanged) and the last page (q_13.9/q_13.10, ends cleanly at the boxed answer with a normal bottom margin, nothing cut off or newly overflowing) via fitz-rendered PNGs. This is a genuine, chapter-content-dependent pagination edge case (this chapter's own content height is unluckily close to a page-boundary multiple) - every other chapter's own content happened to fall far enough inside its last page's boundary that this same latent trailing padding never crossed into an extra page, so the underlying CSS gap was never visible before. Gate re-run after the fix (fitz/PyMuPDF): page count 8 for a 14-item chapter (4 examples + 10 exercises across 5 parts) - sane, not 1, not triple digits. Zero blank pages. Numeric read-back re-run directly against the PDF's own extracted text (mdio.markdown_to_chapter against 06_simplify/chapter.simplified.hi.md, same source stage 9 used, not assumed carried over from the HTML check): all 136 numeric tokens from every question/final_answer field (item- and part-level) found - 0 missing. Applied the documented superscript-exponent-glue guard (inserting a separator before a run of unicode superscript characters before normalizing to ASCII, so a base number and its exponent never merge into one token) defensively, though this chapter's own exponents render as ordinary HTML <sup> spans holding plain ASCII digits rather than literal unicode superscript glyphs, so the specific glued-token failure mode wasn't actually triggered here. Known, unresolved, out-of-scope limitation flagged per step_10/PROMPT.md (not a bug in this chapter's own pipeline output, not a gate failure - the numeric gate only checks digits): Chromium's print-to-PDF pipeline drops the pre-base reph 'र्' from the PDF's *extractable* text layer for every 'र्'+consonant sequence while rendering it correctly on-screen. This chapter uses 'निष्कर्ष' (the conclusion-pill label) 14 times, so copy-pasted or re-extracted text from this PDF will read that word one character short each time; visual rendering is completely unaffected. No fix attempted (documented elsewhere in this project as a Chromium-level defect outside this pipeline's control).

Three errors reported, all confirmed directly against solutions.hi.pdf page renders before any fix. (1) q_13.9 (Coulomb barrier, p.90, प्रश्न 20): the source states the distance between two touching deuteron centres as d=r (should be d=r+r=2r for two touching spheres of radius r), giving a doubled potential energy (720000 eV instead of the correct 360000 eV), then 'corrects' this back down with an ad-hoc, physically unjustified halving step (treating the barrier height as half the computed PE via an energy-conservation argument that doesn't actually apply to what was asked) -- landing on the right final number (360 keV) through two compensating errors rather than correct reasoning. This chapter's own stage 5 (see 05_verify/corrections.md's original q_13.9 entry) had already caught and fixed a DIFFERENT, narrower arithmetic slip in this same solution (a numerator that didn't match its own division on the same line) without noticing the deeper d=r/halving issue underneath it -- that narrower fix is now superseded since this round replaces the derivation it was inside. Corrected: d=2r=4x10^-15 m (touching-sphere contact distance), giving U=(9e9)(1.6e-19)^2/(4e-15)=5.76e-14 J=360000 eV=360 keV directly, with no halving step needed -- the barrier height equals this potential energy itself, per the question's own hint. (2) q_13.2 (Fe-56/Bi-209 binding energy, p.79, प्रश्न 4): the जानकारी states m_p=1.00783 u, m_n=1.00867 u (rounded), but part (i)'s own arithmetic (26.20345, 30.25995) only reproduces if the more precise m_p=1.007825, m_n=1.008665 are used instead -- confirmed by direct recomputation both ways. Part (ii) (Bi-209), in the very same solution, explicitly and correctly writes 1.007825/1.008665. So the source is internally inconsistent about which constant it's using, within one item. The final answers (492.26 MeV/8.790 MeV per nucleon; 1640.26 MeV/7.848 MeV per nucleon) are the correct, well-known official values and were NOT changed -- only the जानकारी box and part (i)'s equation were updated to the precise values actually used, making the item internally consistent with itself and with part (ii). (3) q_13.3 (coin/Cu-63, p.80, प्रश्न 5): the given Cu-63 mass is 62.92960 u (stated in the question itself), but the मान रखो line truncates it to 62.9260 -- confirmed the final answer (0.59225 u) only matches when the full 62.92960 is used, so this was a pure display/transcription slip with no computational impact; fixed the displayed digit to match the question's own stated value and the value actually used.
